title: Novus Analytics - POC scoping: latency SLOs & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping call to define latency & throughput SLOs for Novus Analytics' real-time insights endpoint. Discussed TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, workload sizing, synthetic vs production benchmarks, and a 4-week POC measurement plan. Agreed on next steps: run baseline benchmarks, share security docs, and schedule initial perf test next Tuesday.
action_items: Maya - Share benchmark harness repo and test script - 2027-07-06
Jon - Provide suggested quantization and batching configs for target model - 2027-07-08
Novus (Mark) - Provide representative prompt set and 1-week recent traffic profile - 2027-07-05
Alex - Grant test access to staging VPC OR share sample traffic capture - 2027-07-07
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline tests (cold start + steady state) on selected model
Novus to upload prompt corpus and traffic profile
Schedule 60-min perf test session (warm traffic) next Tuesday 10am PT
Exchange security and SOC2 docs via shared drive
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-07-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Kim (CTO - Novus), Mark Taylor (Eng Lead), Priya Singh (Data Eng), Alex Wu (SRE)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into the latency SLOs and how we want to measure them.
[00:12] Dana Kim: Hi, Dana here. We're trying to define success for the POC 
- main use case is real-time insights API, sub-200ms feels ideal but we know that's ambitious.
[00:24] Mark Taylor: Yeah hi, Mark. Our current infra is a mix of on-prem GPUs and cloud. Key constraints: must hit p95/p99 targets for first token and sustain throughput for burst windows.
[00:36] Jon Ruiz: Great. Quick note on terminology we'll use: TTFT = time to first token (time until first token emitted), TPOT = time per token (average per-token latency during generation). Folks pronounce it differently, sometimes we see T-T-F-T or T-P-O-T in notes.
[00:52] Priya Singh: That matches how we think about SLAs. For short responses (<50 tokens) TTFT dominates user latency. For longer streams TPOT matters.
[01:06] Alex Wu: Also curious about cold vs warm starts 
- our app spins up workers and we need to understand cache/KV warmness impact.

--- Discovery / Requirements ---
[01:30] Maya Patel: Can you share target SLO numbers you have in mind? Dana said sub-200ms, is that p95 or p99?
[01:38] Dana Kim: Initially p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 400ms for TTFT on single-turn queries. If that's impossible for the model family we'll consider relaxed targets or dedicated capacity.
[01:48] Mark Taylor: For TPOT we're thinking p95 <= 40ms/token p99 <= 80ms/token given our avg payloads of 30-60 tokens. Also need end-to-end SLA including network time between our frontend and Redwood's endpoint 
- we'll factor that in.
[02:05] Jon Ruiz: Ok, good. A few clarifications: are you planning to use hosted Redwood API, dedicated Redwood, or private deployment? That changes achievable TTFT.
[02:15] Dana Kim: We'd prefer hosted for ease but open to dedicated if needed for latency. For compliance parts we might need private later but not in the POC.
[02:25] Priya Singh: Our peak QPS is ~120 requests per second across 10 regions, but for POC we want to validate a single-region steady-state and a burst window at 300 RPS for 2-5 minutes.

--- Measurement plan discussion ---
[02:50] Jon Ruiz: Recommended measurement plan: 1) baseline cold-start TTFT measurements with an empty KV cache, 2) steady-state warm measurements after traffic warms the KV cache, 3) token-level TPOT measurement across varying batch sizes (1, 4, 8) and concurrency (1, 8, 32), 4) stress throughput runs to map tokens/sec per GPU and per-node.
[03:12] Mark Taylor: Can we capture p95 and p99 both at request level and token-level? Also distinguish first-byte latency vs total generation time.
[03:20] Jon Ruiz: Yes, we'll instrument both. Best practice is to log: request_received_ts, model_request_sent_ts, first_token_ts, last_token_ts, tokens_generated. From that you can compute TTFT = first_token_ts - model_request_sent_ts, TPOT = (last_token_ts - first_token_ts) / tokens_generated, and throughput = tokens_generated / (last_token_ts - model_request_sent_ts).
[03:45] Alex Wu: FYI our monitoring collects client-side timestamps, so we can align logs. There may be clock skew; we can do sync via NTP and log offsets.

--- SLO targets we discussed ---
[04:10] Maya Patel: Based on similar workloads, realistic POC targets for hosted infra might be: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms; TPOT p95 <= 35-45ms/token, p99 <= 70-90ms/token for a 7B-class model. If you need <200ms p95 TTFT we typically recommend Dedicated pools with pinning or model distillation/quantization.
[04:40] Dana Kim: Noted. For POC let's try to hit TTFT p95 <= 250ms and TPOT p95 <= 45ms/token as the acceptance criteria. If we miss by small margin, acceptable if cost or network accounted for.

--- Workload sizing and benchmarks ---
[05:00] Jon Ruiz: We'll need your prompt distribution and token-length histogram. Priya, can you share sample corpus and typical prompt lengths?
[05:08] Priya Singh: Yes, uploaded a representative 10k prompt corpus earlier today. Most prompts are 20-80 tokens, mean ~35. We'll send a sanitized version as action item.
[05:20] Jon Ruiz: Great. For throughput mapping, plan synthetic runs at concurrency levels: single-client latency tests (1, 2, 4 concurrent), medium load (8, 16), and high burst (32, 64). We'll measure tokens/sec and tail latencies.
[05:40] Mark Taylor: How do batching and KV prefix caching factor in? We have some repeated prefixes in queries.
[05:48] Maya Patel: Redwood's smart batching can group requests but that increases TTFT for small requests if waiting too long. We'll test different batching windows: immediate dispatch, 10ms collect, 50ms collect 
- measure tradeoff between average latency and throughput cost. KV/prefix caching improves TTFT for repeated prompts; we'll run warm cache vs cold cache across the corpus.

--- Measurement harness & artifacts ---
[06:20] Jon Ruiz: We'll provide a benchmark harness (script + docker container) you can run from your staging environment. It will: replay prompts at configurable concurrency with timestamps, collect first-byte and per-token timings, and push results to a CSV and a simple dashboard. We'll share repo link after the call.
[06:38] Dana Kim: Good. For security we need to ensure the harness doesn't send PII. We'll sanitize and run in staging.
[06:45] Maya Patel: We'll also supply sample configs for model choice, quantization profiles, and recommended batch/concurrency knobs.

--- Timeline ---
[07:00] Maya Patel: Proposed 4-week POC timeline:
Week 0 (this week): finalize test corpus, provide credentials -> baseline configs.
Week 1: Baseline benchmarks (cold + warm) and initial tuning.
Week 2: Optimize batching/quantization and run throughput mapping.
Week 3: Run production-like workload, validate metrics, and run perf regression with rollback tests.
Week 4: Finalize results, prepare go/no-go doc, recommendations for dedicated/private if needed.
[07:38] Mark Taylor: That timeline works for us. We need an internal decision by end of week 4.

--- Risks / Objections ---
[08:00] Priya Singh: Concern: network egress from Redwood hosted could add 50-100ms; need to isolate model-only latency.
[08:10] Jon Ruiz: We'll record model-server-side timestamps and provide logs to isolate model latency. For hosted we can do traceroutes and include network time in final report.
[08:22] Alex Wu: Also want to confirm SSO/SSO access for the test accounts and audit logs for requests.
[08:28] Maya Patel: We'll share SOC2 and audit log details; SE will follow up on RBAC and KMS questions.

--- Agreement / Acceptance criteria ---
[08:45] Maya Patel: Recap of acceptance criteria for POC:
- TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms (hosted baseline).
- TPOT p95 <= 45ms/token, p99 <= 90ms/token for typical prompt lengths.
- Throughput mapping: document tokens/sec per GPU and latency at target concurrency (e.g., 120 RPS steady, 300 RPS burst).
- Measurement plan includes cold vs warm cache, batching window tests, and stress throughput runs.

[09:25] Dana Kim: If those are met, we'll move to a pilot for 3 regions with a decision on Dedicated by end of quarter.

--- Closing / Next steps ---
[09:40] Maya Patel: Next: we'll share the benchmark harness repo, Jon will email quantization/batching recommendations, and Mark will upload sanitized prompts and a traffic histogram. Schedule the first perf test Tue 2027-07-06 10am PT.
[09:55] Mark Taylor: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
